questions.prompt: 다음을 듣고, 여자가 하는 말의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: 걷기 프로그램 시간 변경을 안내하려고
방과 후 프로그램 신청을 독려하려고
산책로 출입 금지 시간을 공지하려고
점심 식사 시간 준수를 당부하려고
새로 개설한 동아리를 홍보하려고
questions.script:
W: Good afternoon, students. This is your principal, Ms. Johnson. I’d
like to announce that there has been a change of schedule for our
weekly walking program, Step Together. It was originally supposed
to take place every Monday after school, starting next week.
However, it seems that many students are busy with club activities
after school. Therefore, in order to allow more students to
participate, it’ll now be held at 1 p.m. during lunchtime. We hope
this change gives you the opportunity to enjoy meaningful moments
with your friends. We look forward to seeing you there!

questions.prompt: 대화를 듣고, 남자의 의견으로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: 냉장고 문을 자주 여닫으면 전기가 낭비된다.
과도한 육류 섭취는 영양 불균형의 원인이 된다.
한 번 해동한 음식은 다시 냉동하지 않는 것이 좋다.
음식을 밀폐해서 보관하면 세균 증식을 억제할 수 있다.
오랫동안 냉동 보관한 음식을 먹는 것은 해로울 수 있다.
questions.script:
W: Honey, how about having beef for dinner tonight? We have some in
the freezer.
M: Great idea, but that beef has been in the freezer for so long. We’d
better not eat it.
W: Well, it’s been frozen this whole time, so it should be fine.
M: Not really. Eating food that’s been kept frozen for a long time can
be harmful.
W: Really? I thought it would be alright.
M: Well, while freezing can slow bacteria growth in food, it cannot
completely stop them from growing.
W: Hmm, that makes sense.
M: Besides, if we open the freezer often, the temperature inside doesn’t
stay constant.
W: Oh. That might also encourage bacteria growth.
M: Correct! That’s why it can be harmful to eat food that’s been stored
frozen for a long time.
W: I see. Let’s go grocery shopping for some beef then.

questions.prompt: 다음을 듣고, 남자가 하는 말의 요지로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choices: 무선 이어폰의 장시간 사용은 청력에 부정적인 영향을 미친다.
무선 이어폰은 주변 소음을 차단하여 집중력을 높일 수 있다.
보행 중 무선 이어폰 사용은 심각한 사고를 유발할 수 있다.
자전거를 탈 때 보행자를 배려하는 습관이 필요하다.
운동을 하면서 음악을 들으면 운동 효과가 커진다.
questions.script:
M: Hello, listeners. This is Life Advice for All. Nowadays, many people
are using wireless earphones, especially while walking, because
they’re convenient to use. However, this could cause serious
accidents. If you are only paying attention to music or other media
in your wireless earphones, you might not hear your surrounding
sounds. This can prevent you from recognizing and reacting to
dangerous situations. For example, you may not notice when cars
are coming towards you or when bicycles are passing by. For your
own safety, please think twice about using wireless earphones when
you’re walking. I’ll be back with some more useful advice next time.

questions.prompt: 대화를 듣고, 그림에서 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.
questions.script:
M: Honey, I just finished setting up the rooftop garden party for
tomorrow. Have a look!
W: That’s fantastic!
M: I’m glad you like it. I put the party banner above the door. What do
you think?
W: Perfect. And the striped sun umbrella is between the chairs.
M: I hope it’ll give us enough shade.
W: Me too. Where did you get the lamp on the table?
M: I picked it up at the mall the other day. Its light creates a warm
atmosphere at night.
W: Lovely. I also like the two flowerpots next to the wall.
M: Those are gifts from my friends.
W: That’s so kind of them. The round rug on the floor looks cozy and
comfortable.
M: Yes, it’s for the kids. They can sit and play on it.
W: Great. Let’s make the party unforgettable.

questions.prompt: 대화를 듣고, 여자가 할 일로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

questions.script:
M: Hey, Emily. The school art gallery event is only two weeks away.
Is everything on track?
W: Hi, Jake. I think so. Let’s go over the to­do list.
M: Good idea. Did we decide on the location?
W: Yes, we’re using the art room. It’ll be turned into the gallery.
M: Awesome. How about the invitation emails?
W: I sent them out last week. Most guests already said that they’ll
come.
M: Great! And the event pamphlets are being printed. They’ll be ready
in a few days.
W: Wonderful. Have you chosen the background music?
M: Yeah, we’ll go with classical music.
W: That’s perfect. I think that would match the mood.
M: We still need to buy gifts for the guests.
W: That’s on me. I’ll take care of it.
M: Thanks. I appreciate it.

questions.prompt: 대화를 듣고, 남자가 지불할 금액을 고르시오.
questions.script:
W: Welcome to the Pet Hotel! How may I help you?
M: Hi! I’m thinking of leaving my dog here for a couple of days. I’ll be
out of town for a business trip.
W: Alright! Exactly how long will your dog be staying here?
M: Three nights. How much does it usually cost?
W: It’s $40 per night. But if your dog is large, you’ll be charged an
additional $10 per night.
M: Luckily, my dog is a small Maltese.
W: Then, you don’t have to pay the extra fee. Will you need our
pick­up service? It costs $30.
M: Yes, please. That’d be nice.
W: Okay. Is it your first time here? If that’s the case, you can get a
10% discount off the total price.
M: That’s great! Yes, it’s my first time here.
W: Alright. How would you like to pay?
M: Here’s my credit card.

questions.script:
M: Sarah, have you heard about the special lecture at the community
center this Saturday?
W: Yeah, Brian. It’s a lecture on how to design effective presentation
materials, right?
M: Exactly! It’ll help you create impressive presentations. Do you want
to sign up for it with me?
W: I’d love to, but I can’t attend.
M: Oh. Is it because you have a part­time job on weekends?
W: No. I don’t work on weekends anymore.
M: Hmm. Then, do you have to work on your physics assignment?
W: I already finished it. Actually, I’m participating in a volleyball
match.
M: Really? You told me that you wouldn’t play this time, didn’t you?
W: I’m filling in for Judy. She injured her knee last week.
M: I see. Good luck!

questions.script:

M: No, I haven’t. Do people wear historical costumes at the parade?
W: That’s right. It’s a good chance to experience wearing costumes
from different eras.
M: Sounds interesting. Where will it take place?
W: It’ll be held at Central City Park.
M: Okay. What’s this event for?
W: Its main purpose is to celebrate the city’s cultural heritage, and to
inform people about its history.
M: That’s a great idea. When is it?
W: October 11th. I saw an advertisement for it yesterday, and I signed
up to be a costumed participant.
M: Awesome. Can I sign up for it, too?
W: Yeah. You have to fill out the registration form on the city’s official
website.
M: Perfect. I’ll do that right away.

questions.prompt: 2025 Brain Competition에 관한 다음 내용을 듣고, 일치하지 않는 것을 고르시오.
choices: 고등학생을 대상으로 한다.

questions.script:
M: Hello, students! The 2025 Brain Competition is coming up! This is
an annual neuroscience competition for high school students. It’ll be
held on Saturday, September 13th, at the City Neuroscience Center.
It’ll last for three hours, beginning at 10 a.m. and ending at 1 p.m.
The competition will consist of two rounds. For the first round,
contestants will take a written exam, and the top nine contestants
will advance to the next round. For the second round, the remaining
students will take an oral exam in front of three judges. Please
remember that the usage of electronic devices is not permitted
during the competition. The winner will get a $500 cash prize and a
chance to compete in the national competition. Join us for this
exciting challenge!

questions.script:
M: Jack and Emma are close friends. Emma invites Jack to join her at
a local charity flea market this upcoming weekend. While Emma has
participated in flea markets several times before, Jack is new to
this kind of event. He’s looking forward to it, and excitedly
searches for items to sell. But he wonders what kinds of things

about what kinds of items would be popular at flea markets. In this

W: Hello, students. As you know, animals build many different
structures in the natural world. Today, we’ll talk about the different
functions that these structures have. First, an important function of
animal­built structures is to provide protection from predators. For
example, beavers build dams to create ponds where they can
construct their homes. These structures provide a shelter from
predators. Next, animal structures can also play a role in
transportation. Some species of ants use their own bodies to create
bridges. These bridges provide a path over obstacles and allow
them to search for food at an increased speed. In addition, animal
structures can serve as traps. This can be observed in web­building
spiders, who weave elaborate webs of sticky spider silk that
capture prey. Finally, animal structures can serve as a means of
attracting mates. During mating season, some species of birds
collect small branches, leaves, and colorful objects to create
structures that attract the attention of females. Now, let’s watch a
short video about these incredible animal structures.
